\CourseData{1120}{title}{Precalculus with Review I}
\CourseData{1120}{credits}{5 credits}
\CourseData{1120}{semesters}{Autumn}
\CourseData{1120}{description}{This is the first course of a two course sequence covering precalculus. \CourseData{5631}{prereq}{A grade of C$-$ or above in 5630. Open only to Actuarial Science majors, and to MMS students specializing in Financial Math.}
\CourseData{5631}{lastoffered}{Spring 2027}
%% Math 5632
\CourseData{5632}{title}{Financial Economics for Actuaries}
\CourseData{5632}{credits}{3 credits}
\CourseData{5632}{semesters}{Autumn, Spring, Summer}
\CourseData{5632}{description}{Introduction to the evaluation of options, futures, and other derivatives, interest models and risk management techniques. Includes material from examinations by the Society of Actuaries and the Casualty Actuarial Society.}
\CourseData{5632}{prereq}{A grade of C$-$ or above in 3618; and a grade of C$-$ or above in 4530, 5530H, or Stat 4201; and enrollment in Math major or Actuarial Science major or Actuarial Science Pre-major, or Grad standing; or permission of department.}
\CourseData{5632}{lastoffered}{Spring 2027}
%% Math 5633
\CourseData{5633}{title}{Loss Models I}
\CourseData{5633}{credits}{3 credits}
\CourseData{5633}{semesters}{Autumn, Spring}
\CourseData{5633}{description}{Introduction to the construction and evaluation of actuarial models, with topics covered by examinations of the Society of Actuaries and the Casualty Actuarial Society.}
\CourseData{5633}{prereq}{A C$-$ or above in Stat 4202; and a C$-$ or above in 4530, 5530H, or Stat 4201. Open only to actuarial science majors, and to MMS students specializing in Financial Math.}
\CourseData{5633}{lastoffered}{Autumn 2026}
%% Math 5634
\CourseData{5634}{title}{Loss Models II}
\CourseData{5634}{credits}{3 credits}
\CourseData{5634}{semesters}{Spring}
\CourseData{5634}{description}{Continuation of 5633: introduction to the construction and evaluation of actuarial models, with topics covered by examinations of the Society of Actuaries and the Casualty Actuarial Society.}
\CourseData{5634}{prereq}{C$-$ or better in 5633. Open only to actuarial science majors, and to MMS students specializing in Financial Math.}
\CourseData{5634}{lastoffered}{Spring 2027}
%% Math 5635
\CourseData{5635}{title}{Stochastic Calculus for Finance I}
\CourseData{5635}{credits}{3 credits}
\CourseData{5635}{semesters}{Autumn}
\CourseData{5635}{description}{Mathematics used in financial asset pricing, based on Wiener (Brownian motion) processes, with applications. Overview of needed real analysis, stochastic processes, Ito Calculus, Risk-neutral measure, connections with PDEs.}
\CourseData{5635}{prereq}{A grade of C$-$ or above in 3589 or 3345; and a grade of C$-$ or above in 4530, 5530H, or Stat 4201; and enrollment in Math major or Actuarial Science major; or Grad standing; or permission of department.}
\CourseData{5635}{lastoffered}{Autumn 2026}
%% Math 5636
\CourseData{5636}{title}{Stochastic Calculus for Finance II}
\CourseData{5636}{credits}{3 credits}
\CourseData{5636}{semesters}{Spring}
\CourseData{5636}{description}{Continuation of 5635. Feynman-Kac theorem, diffusion with drift, applications to problems in financial mathematics.}
\CourseData{5636}{prereq}{A grade of C$-$ or above in 5635; and enrollment in Math major or Actuarial Science major, or Grad standing; or permission of department.}
\CourseData{5636}{lastoffered}{Spring 2027}
%% Math 5637
\CourseData{5637}{title}{Topics in Predictive Modeling}
\CourseData{5637}{credits}{3 credits}
\CourseData{5637}{semesters}{Autumn, Spring}
\CourseData{5637}{description}{An introduction to some basic concepts and methods in statistical learning with emphasis on the mathematics behind these concepts and methods.}
\CourseData{5637}{prereq}{A grade of C$-$ or above in 2568 or 5520H, and a grade of C$-$ or above in Stat 4202; or permission of department.}
\CourseData{5637}{lastoffered}{Spring 2027}
%% Math 5638
\CourseData{5638}{title}{Topics in Risk Modeling II}
\CourseData{5638}{credits}{3 credits}
\CourseData{5638}{semesters}{Spring}
\CourseData{5638}{description}{Risk Modeling is an important area of Actuarial Science, which is based on statistical or machine learning and the underlying mathematics. Math 5637: Topics in Risk Modeling I offers an introduction to these topics, and Math 5638, as the second course in this sequence, covers more advanced machine learning models with a focus on mathematics and theories.}
\CourseData{5638}{prereq}{2568 or equiv.; and 5637; and 4530 or Stat 4201; and STAT 4202; or permission of department.}
\CourseData{5638}{lastoffered}{Spring 2027}
%% Math 5651
\CourseData{5651}{title}{Mathematical Modeling of Biological Processes}
\CourseData{5651}{credits}{3 credits}
\CourseData{5651}{semesters}{Spring}
\CourseData{5651}{description}{Enzyme dynamics, predator-prey and competition model, spread of diseases, plant growth, cell cycle and cell differentiation, reaction-diffusion with advection, cancer models and cancer therapy, wound healing.}
\CourseData{5651}{prereq}{Grad standing; or either 4512 (512) or 557, and 4556 (556), and either 2568 (568) or 572.}
\CourseData{5651}{exclusions}{Not open to students with credit for 865.}

\CourseData{6251}{credits}{4 credits}
\CourseData{6251}{semesters}{Autumn}
\CourseData{6251}{description}{Review of measures and integration; independence for events and for random variables; covariance and correlation for random variables; weak and strong laws of large numbers; Borel-Cantelli lemmas; Central Limit Theorems.}
\CourseData{6251}{prereq}{5202 (653).}
\CourseData{6251}{exclusions}{Not open to students with credit for 722.}
\CourseData{6251}{lastoffered}{Autumn 2026}

\CourseData{6252}{credits}{4 credits}
\CourseData{6252}{semesters}{Spring}
\CourseData{6252}{description}{Central limit theorems; Poisson processes; random walks, Markov chains; martingales; Brownian motion; stochastic processes.}
\CourseData{6252}{prereq}{6251 (723).}
\CourseData{6252}{exclusions}{Not open to students with credit for 724.}
\CourseData{6252}{lastoffered}{Spring 2027}
%% Math 6411
\CourseData{6411}{title}{Ordinary Differential Equations I}
\CourseData{6411}{credits}{3 credits}
\CourseData{6411}{semesters}{Autumn}
\CourseData{6411}{description}{Existence, uniqueness and smooth dependence; linear systems; periodic and homoclinic orbits; stability, hyperbolicity; stable, unstable, and center invariant manifolds; bifurcations of equilibria and periodic orbits; chaos, strange attractors.}
\CourseData{6411}{prereq}{Both 5202 and either 2568 (568) or 572.}
\CourseData{6411}{exclusions}{Not open to students with credit for Math 715.}
\CourseData{6411}{lastoffered}{Autumn 2026}

\CourseData{6451}{credits}{3 credits}
\CourseData{6451}{semesters}{Spring}

\CourseData{6451}{exclusions}{Not open to students with credit for 717.}
\CourseData{6451}{lastoffered}{Spring 2027}

\CourseData{6501}{credits}{3 credits}
\CourseData{6501}{semesters}{Autumn}
\CourseData{6501}{description}{Enumerative combinatorics: factorials, binomials and multinomials, Stirling approximation, recursion and generating functions, Catalan numbers. Graph theory: Kuratowksi's theorem, graph coloring, Ramsey theory, matrix-tree theorem, expander graphs.}
\CourseData{6501}{prereq}{Grad standing in Math; or 4581 and 2568; or permission of instructor.}
\CourseData{6501}{lastoffered}{Autumn 2026}

\CourseData{6502}{credits}{3 credits}
\CourseData{6502}{semesters}{Spring}
\CourseData{6502}{description}{Ramsey theory, extremal graph theory. First moment method, second moment method, alterations. Concentration inequalities. Lovasz local lemma. Martingale methods. Correlation inequalities. Phase transitions. Random trees, random planar maps.}
\CourseData{6502}{prereq}{6501 or permission of instructor.}
\CourseData{6502}{lastoffered}{Spring 2027}

\CourseData{7452.02}{description}{Sobolev spaces, Sobolev inequalities and embedding theorems; Lax-Milgram theorem, Fredholm alternatives, weak compactness; linear elliptic equations: existence, regularity, maximum principles; hyperbolic equations; first order hyperbolic systems.}
\CourseData{7452.02}{prereq}{Post-candidacy in Math, and permission of instructor. This course is graded S/U.}
\CourseData{7452.02}{lastoffered}{Autumn 2026}

\CourseData{7611}{title}{Computational Partial Differential Equations I}
\CourseData{7611}{credits}{3 credits}
\CourseData{7611}{semesters}{Autumn}
\CourseData{7611}{description}{Numerical methods for boundary value problems (BVP); extension to separable elliptic PDEs, fast solvers; irregular domains, variable coefficients; iterative methods; diffusion equations; error analysis; variable coefficients in nonlinear problems.}
\CourseData{7611}{prereq}{6602 (709).}
\CourseData{7611}{exclusions}{Not open to students with credit for 807.}
\CourseData{7611}{lastoffered}{Autumn 2026}
%% Math 7612
\CourseData{7612}{title}{Computational Partial Differential Equations II}
\CourseData{7612}{credits}{3 credits}
\CourseData{7612}{semesters}{Spring}
\CourseData{7612}{description}{Linear hyperbolic equations, finite difference methods; quasi-linear and non-linear equations with shock formation, Lax-Wendroff theorem; flux-limiters, WENO methods; multi-dimensional problems; transport equations; adaptive grids, grid generation.}
\CourseData{7612}{prereq}{7611 (808).}
\CourseData{7612}{exclusions}{Not open to students with credit for 809.}
\CourseData{7612}{lastoffered}{Spring 2027}
